title: 不要忧虑 Do Not Be Anxious — 马太福音 6:25–34

sections.heading: 不要忧虑 Do Not Be Anxious
body: 马太福音 6:25–34 · Matthew 6:25–34
周五小组 Friday Small Group · 2026-10-02

sections.heading: 经文 Scripture — 马太福音 6:25–34 Matthew
sections.keyPhrase: 「不要为生命忧虑」 “Do not worry about your life” (v.25)

verses.cuv: 「所以我告诉你们，不要为生命忧虑吃甚么，喝甚么；为身体忧虑穿甚么。生命不胜于饮食么？身体不胜于衣裳么？
verses.en: Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?

verses.cuv: 你们看那天上的飞鸟，也不种，也不收，也不积蓄在仓里，你们的天父尚且养活他。你们不比飞鸟贵重得多吗？
verses.en: Look at the birds of the air: They do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?

verses.cuv: 你们那一个能用思虑使寿数多加一刻呢〔或作：使身量多加一肘呢〕？
verses.en: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?

verses.cuv: 何必为衣裳忧虑呢？你想野地里的百合花怎么长起来；它也不劳苦，也不纺线。
verses.en: And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.

verses.cuv: 然而我告诉你们，就是所罗门极荣华的时候，他所穿戴的，还不如这花一朵呢！
verses.en: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.

verses.cuv: 你们这小信的人哪！野地里的草今天还在，明天就丢在炉里，神还给它这样的妆饰，何况你们呢！
verses.en: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?

verses.cuv: 所以，不要忧虑说：吃甚么？喝甚么？穿甚么？
verses.en: Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’

verses.cuv: 这都是外邦人所求的，你们需用的这一切东西，你们的天父是知道的。
verses.en: For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.

verses.cuv: 你们要先求他的国和他的义，这些东西都要加给你们了。
verses.en: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you.

verses.cuv: 所以，不要为明天忧虑，因为明天自有明天的忧虑；一天的难处一天当就彀了。」
verses.en: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.

sections.heading: 背景 Context
body: 属于登山宝训 · Part of the Sermon on the Mount.
第25节的「所以」承接 vv.19–24：积财宝在天上，「一个人不能事奉两个主——神和玛门」 · The “therefore” in v.25 hangs on vv.19–24: treasures in heaven, “no one can serve two masters — God and money.”
耶稣所针对的忧虑，来自事奉了错误的主 · The anxiety Jesus addresses results from serving the wrong master.
听众多是务农糊口的人——吃穿是每天实在的难处 · His audience were subsistence farmers — food and clothing were real daily uncertainties.
这是对不安稳之人的信靠功课，不是对安逸之人的劝勉 · This is trust taught to the insecure, not advice to the comfortable.

sections.heading: 原文 Original Language
body: μεριμνάω (merimnaō)——被挂虑撕扯、心思分裂；与马大「思虑烦扰」同源（路加福音 10:41） · to be pulled apart by care, divided in mind; same root as Martha “anxious and troubled” (Luke 10:41).
现在时态：「停止忧虑」——是要破除的习惯 · Present tense: “stop being anxious” — a habit to break.
merimnaō 也可以是好的——保罗用它形容提摩太挂念教会（腓立比书 2:20） · Note merimnaō can be good — Paul uses it for Timothy’s care for the church (Philippians 2:20).
问题不在于你是否在乎，而在于什么把你撕裂 · The issue is what divides you, not whether you care.

sections.heading: 交叉经文 Cross-references
body: 路加福音 12:22–31 · Luke 12:22–31 — 平行经文；「你们这小群，不要惧怕」 · parallel; “little flock, fear not”
腓立比书 4:6–7 · Philippians 4:6–7 — 替代之道：祷告加感恩 → 平安 · the replacement: prayer with thanksgiving → peace
彼得前书 5:7 · 1 Peter 5:7 — 「将一切的忧虑卸给神」 · “cast all your anxiety on him”
诗篇 55:22 · Psalm 55:22 — 旧约根源 · OT root
马太福音 6:19–24 · Matthew 6:19–24 — 忧虑的起因，就在前文 · the cause, immediately before

sections.heading: 讨论 Discussion
questions: 这一周，忧虑实际出现在哪里？说出最主要的一两个。 · Where does anxiety actually show up in your week? Name the top one or two.
耶稣把忧虑与「事奉两个主」连在一起（vv.24–25）。你最大的忧虑背后，有没有一个「财宝」？ · Jesus ties anxiety to “serving two masters” (vv.24–25). Is there a treasure behind your top anxiety?
merimnaō 的意思是「被撕扯、分裂」。具体来说，负责任的计划与心被撕裂，差别在哪里？ · merimnaō means “pulled apart, divided.” What is the difference, concretely, between responsible planning and being divided?

v.33「先求他的国」——如果忧虑只有在中心关注改变时才会缩小，那在你第一题提到的处境里，「先求」会是什么样子？ · v.33 “seek first the kingdom” — if anxiety shrinks only when the central concern changes, what would “seeking first” look like in the situation you named in Q1?

腓立比书 4:6–7 给出替代的习惯。本周你真能持守的一个操练是什么？从生活应用菜单里选一个，并告诉一个人你选了哪个。 · Philippians 4:6–7 gives the replacement habit. What is one practice you could actually keep this week? Pick it from the Life menu and tell one person which you chose.

rows.practice: 固定的睡前程序：放下手机 + 读太6:34 + 定点熄灯，坚持五晚 · Fixed wind-down: phone away + Matthew 6:34 + lights out at a set time, 5 nights.
把你最大的忧虑告诉一位信任的人，请他为此祷告一次 · Tell one trusted person your top anxiety; ask them to pray for it once.
一顿饭的时间，每人说一次神在忧虑中供应的经历 · One meal where each person names a time God provided when they worried.
把忧虑写下来，标注「今天的还是明天的？」（v.34），把明天的留在纸上 · Write the worry down, mark “today’s or tomorrow’s?” (v.34), park tomorrow’s on paper.
腓4:6 反应操练：忧虑一起来，就说一句祈求加一句感恩 · Philippians 4:6 reflex: one sentence of request + one of thanksgiving each time anxiety rises.
检视一项为了安抚忧虑而存在的固定开支，做个决定 · Review one recurring expense that exists to quiet anxiety; decide about it.
每天用 v.33 祷告：「今天先求神的国是什么样子？」——每早写下一行 · Pray v.33 daily: “what does seeking first look like today?” — one written line each morning.

sections.heading: 反思 Reflection
body: 周二跟进：操练做了吗？什么拦阻了它？ · Tuesday check-in: did the practice happen? What blocked it?
周四跟进：忧虑上来时，操练有没有改变你接下来的行动？ · Thursday check-in: when anxiety rose, did the practice change what you did next?
周末回顾：用你自己的话说，你里面有什么改变？ · End of week: what changed in you, in your own words?
